questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very important that the country I would study in had to have english as their main language. Furthermore, I took exchange as an opportunity to go very far away and explore a culture on the other side of the planet.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is definitely worth going on exchange!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host-university gave a lot of information prior to my arrival. However, it is quite difficult to get information about which specific units, that you can choose between at Deakin - A lot of them either were on the wrong campus or in the wrong trimester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help to find a place to live in Melbourne and how to create an account on the different websites for Deakin.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can either live alone, with one other or with 4-6 others. However, the 4-6 other was definitely the cheapest option.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans were available. Stoves, ovens, fridge and refrigerator was available but not any of the items for the kitchen. However, that can be bought very cheap at a K-mart nearby.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It has some cons and benefits. 

Benefits: 
- I found a lot of friends on campus housing.
- The team behind the housing hosts a lot of events where you can meet other people.
- It was very easy and convenient not having to find housing in Melbourne. 
- It is close to your classes.

Cons:
- You are not close to Melbourne city. it takes about an hour to get into the city.
- The rooms and facilities are not cozy - So I would bring some pictures or something to make it more personal. 
- There is.a long way to grocery shopping.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to find the units online at their website - It seemed like quite a jungle in the start. Then you have to apply and you get allocated different units. From there you wish for specific timetables and hopefully get your wish fulfilled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could go to Student Assistance at Deakin, their exchange information or write an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the units I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only chose units without an exam in order to make it possible to travel around afterwards - You can find information about the different units exams at when you click on them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is not very high in Australia. They often did not expect a lot from you and if you put in the hours you dont have to worry about passing or not.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was no physical lectures at Deakin - Everything was prerecorded. We had class teaching which were kind of similar to the ones at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Introduction to Public Relations
- Health Communication
- Fundamentals of Health Informatics
- Program Planning, Management, and Evaluation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Program Planning, Management, and Evaluation had a good teacher and teaching-style. Furthermore, the content of the course were very public health relevant. 

Health Communication was a good unit as well with lots of examples from the real world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The health insurance in Australia is mandatory.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery and living prices are very expensive in Melbourne. Coffee and eating is cheaper than Denmark but not much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a lot of clubs, but it is often very hard to join when you are only there for one trimester. Furthermore, a lot of times the clubs met up every friday night which made it hard to attend other social gatherings and being a part of the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports clubs including the runners club, basketball, tennis, Australian football, soccer etc. However, as mentioned before it is often hard to join as an exchange student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the runners club which was a cozy and chill club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Take a lot of weekend trips from Melbourne! Especially Tasmania and Sydney is a must-do. I also went to Mornington peninsula, and great ocean road in the weekends.   

On the holiday I drove the east coast from Brisbane to Cairns. 

Furthermore, use the city as much as possible - Go to Fitzroy and Richmond espeically

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy - People are friendly and only wants the best for you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the clubs availiable and have an open attitudes in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Often Australians are not very effective - They take a long time doing stuff. But other than that it is very similar to the danish culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people from Australia is much more open-minded and friendly than the Danish. Furthermore, they have a more chilled and laid back attitude towards a lot of things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Deakin is not in the main city of Melbourne.
- Do not worry to much about school. 
- Have a good time!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a bit more expensive than expected so use the time to apply for a lot of scholarships.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made - I love that I have made lots of international connections and I have improved my english so much being down here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: People being so far away from you - It is hard being alone in another country and having to make friends from scratch.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
